claim: Guotai Junan Securities, '基于短周期价量特征的多因子选股体系——数量化专题之九十三' (A Multi-Factor Stock Selection System Based on Short-Cycle Price-Volume Characteristics -- Quantitative Special Report No. 93), June 2017. This is the origin research report defining all 191 GTJA Alpha191 formulas (ids 001-191); every secondary source below is a replication/documentation of this report, not the report itself.
impact_on_spec: Confirms the 191-formula report's title/scope/date for provenance; the PDF itself was not directly fetched/parsed this round (found via search, not opened) -- all 14 new formulas implemented this round (ids 039/046/049/054/063/071/073/084/086/123/155/161/184/190) were sourced from the secondary/tertiary replications below and cross-checked against each other, not against this PDF directly.
limitations: Not directly opened this round; provenance-only citation. If any formula below is later found to disagree with this original PDF, the PDF is authoritative, not the secondary sources.

claim: Daic115/alpha191 (raw.githubusercontent.com/Daic115/alpha191/master/alpha191.py, the same repo already used and disclosed for the original 20-id round -- no LICENSE file, not vendored), fetched via WebFetch (content passed through a summarizing model, not raw bytes) for ids 039/046/049/054/063/071/073/084/086/123/155/161/184/190. Used only as one of three independent formula-text cross-checks, NOT as a code source -- WebFetch's summarization was caught introducing real transcription errors in this exact fetch: alpha_086's branch logic was inverted relative to its own quoted docstring (the -1 and close-diff-term branches were swapped) and alpha_073's returned code distributed the formula's outer *-1 over only one of its two terms instead of both, both contradicted by two independent formula-text sources (claims gtja191_channelcmt_wiki_formulas and gtja191_bigquant_wiki_formulas below, which agree with each other). This module's actual implementation follows the verified formula TEXT, never this fetch's code.
impact_on_spec: Formula-text cross-check input only (1 of 3 sources); its DECAYLINEAR helper definition (weights window..1 normalized to sum 1, applied via rolling.apply) matches the standard DECAYLINEAR semantic in the abstract, but a literal port of its exact array construction into this repo's sliding_window_view-based implementation would have put the largest weight on the OLDEST day in each window, not today -- caught by this repo's own test (test_decay_linear_weights_the_most_recent_observation_most) before any alpha used the primitive; see _panel_ops.decay_linear's docstring for the full reasoning. Not copied verbatim for that reason. Its own alpha_054 default (STD window tied to the correlation window, 10) informed the alpha054 window-ambiguity interpretation (see gtja191_alpha054_std_window_ambiguity below).
limitations: WebFetch-summarized, not raw code read directly -- demonstrated unreliable for exact branch/sign logic in this fetch (086, 073); treated as formula-text-only evidence, weighted below the two sources that independently agree with each other (BigQuant, ChannelCMT/OFO wiki).

Independently agrees with claim gtja191_bigquant_wiki_formulas on every formula's structure, including alpha054's exact bracketing (StdDev(Abs(close-open),5) -- note: this source gives an explicit window of 5, one of two disagreeing explicit-window claims found this round, see gtja191_alpha054_std_window_ambiguity) and alpha073/alpha184's exact sign placement.

Corroborates the structural shape of alpha039/046/049/054/063/071/084/123/155/161/184 against the two wiki sources above. Notably its own code for alpha073 and alpha181 both explicitly return 0 / are left unimplemented ('Returns 0 (unimplemented)') despite the formula text being present -- independent evidence (alongside the Daic115 code's need to redefine BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE as a cross-sectional mean return rather than an actual index level, see gtja191_alpha181_benchmarkindexclose_blocked) that alpha181 is a known-hard-to-implement formula in the open community, not just to this repo.

claim: alpha054's original formula is quoted identically in structure by all three formula-text sources as '-1 * RANK((STD(ABS(CLOSE-OPEN)[, window]) + (CLOSE-OPEN)) + CORR(CLOSE,OPEN,10))', but the STD term's window is given inconsistently: BigQuant's literal string omits any explicit window ('STD(ABS(CLOSE -OPEN))'); ChannelCMT/OFO wiki gives an explicit window of 5; the Daic115 reference code implicitly uses the same window as CORR's explicit 10 (a single corr_period=10 parameter drives both). This is judged a genuine ambiguity in the underlying report text (not a fetch error), consistent with this file's existing documented practice of disclosing formula corrections/interpretations rather than silently picking one.
impact_on_spec: This repo's gtja054 implementation uses STD window=10 (tied to the formula's only other explicit window, CORR's 10) -- the Daic115 interpretation -- documented explicitly in alpha191.py's module docstring and the gtja054 inline comment as a disclosed interpretation choice, not a verified single answer. Re-derivable IC/backtest sensitivity to this choice is a known caveat for gtja054 specifically, to be disclosed in the Step 15 report chapter.
limitations: No source directly resolves this ambiguity; a 5-day-window variant was not implemented or compared this round due to time budget -- flagged as a possible follow-up sensitivity check, not resolved here.

claim: alpha181's formula (BigQuant literal text: 'SUM(((CLOSE/DELAY(CLOSE,1)-1)-MEAN((CLOSE/DELAY(CLOSE,1)-1),20))-(BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE-MEAN(BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE,20))^2,20)/SUM((BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE-MEAN(BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE,20))^3)') requires a 'BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE' (sic; benchmark index close) input this repo's alpha191 pipeline does not carry (compute_alpha191's PANEL_FIELDS are open/high/low/close/volume/vwap only, no index/benchmark series). Its semantics are also genuinely ambiguous across sources: if BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE is literally the benchmark's raw price level (e.g. CSI300 close, ~3000-4000), squaring/cubing its demeaned value and adding/dividing it against a demeaned-RETURN-scale term ((close/delay(close,1)-1), ~0.01 scale) is dimensionally inconsistent, suggesting either a report typo or that the term is actually meant to be a benchmark RETURN, not a price level. The only source that provides a working implementation (Daic115, see gtja191_daic115_fetch_ids_39_190) resolves this by silently redefining BANCHMARKINDEXCLOSE as the cross-sectional mean of every stock's own daily return (not an external index series at all) -- an unstated modeling substitution, not a literal transcription. Two of three independent sources (kangchihlun gist, effectively BigQuant's own text-only presentation) do not provide a working implementation at all for this id.
impact_on_spec: alpha181 (gtja181) is NOT implemented this round -- moved to alpha191.py's _FETCHED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED with this reasoning, per this project's explicit rule to document a genuine blocker rather than encode an ambiguous/guessed interpretation into a factor that would silently feed every downstream screen and backtest. This repo already has a precedent for substituting SPY as a single-factor market proxy when a formula needs a benchmark/index term the panel lacks (osap_price.py's DEFAULT_MARKET_SYMBOL), but that precedent does not resolve which of the two structurally different interpretations above (price-level vs. return) is the one the original report intended, and the wrong choice would silently corrupt this one column across the whole screen -- judged not worth guessing. The US-17 report chapter reports this id as not-implemented/blocked rather than omitting it from the US-17 comparison table.
limitations: Blocked on formula-semantics ambiguity plus a real data-plumbing gap (no benchmark series wired into compute_alpha191), not on inability to find any source at all -- if a future round resolves the semantics (e.g. by locating the original PDF's exact wording, claim gtja191_origin_report_2017) this can be revisited.
